title: Intra-CTA split-K with warp-specialized TMA producers is expressible today; what is not is a cross-CTA partial plus a declared merge, and the corpus I offered as evidence has no contrast for it

evidence.note: No open-cake-ir campaign and no device. This record exists partly to retract a count I stated before applying the independence rule below.

ReductionScope has one member, CTA. OnlineSoftmaxParameters takes that scope, so the two-kernel decomposition every retained attention decode kernel uses -- partial outputs plus LSE, then a merge kernel combining them -- has no spelling. The gap is real and independent of any corpus.

After separating authoring arms and counting only mechanisms a candidate ADDED to its seed: optimize_existing/attn has 53 candidates and ZERO that added split-K, because the 012/014/015 seeds already contain it -- one observation shared by 53 candidates, not 53. clean_start/attn has 8 candidates on one task from 4 workflows and ALL EIGHT contain split-K, so there is no without-group and no contrast. optimize_existing/gemm is the only measured contrast in the corpus: 77 added it across 5 tasks and 9 workflows, median 1.012x against 198 without at 1.040x, delta -0.029.

Corroborating and also negative, measured on B200: split-K with atomic_add into an fp32 accumulator plus a separate cast kernel reads 0.27-0.28x at M=11948/14104 and 0.155x at M=901 for skinny-N GEMM, attributed to two extra launches and a 14.4 MB fp32 buffer; a two-pass split-K plus fp32 partial reduce reads 0.7541x at K=4096/N=6144.

Found by probing the Compiler rather than by reading the vocabulary, and it narrows this record twice over. That schedule declares three roles -- one compute plus two producers -- loads both operands with movement 'tma' on the producer roles, accumulates into a shared-memory `partial_accumulators` buffer and folds it with `reduce` at scope 'cta'. So split-K, warp specialization and TMA staging are each expressible today, together, in one Schedule. What 012's retained kernels do instead is split across CTAs -- grid (kv_heads, batch, NUM_SPLITS) writing partial outputs plus LSE, then a second kernel launch merging them by online softmax. That is the part with no spelling: ReductionScope admits only CTA, and a Schedule materializes one kernel.

observation: I previously reported this corpus as supplying a +11.54 attention delta for split-K. That number came from pooling two authoring arms and comparing across tasks with different baselines. Under the independence rule the corpus is built to support -- candidates sharing a seed are not independent observations of what the seed contains -- the attention evidence collapses to a single seed on one arm and a zero-contrast group of eight on the other. What survives is the opposite sign, on GEMM, from two independent sources. The IR gap does not go away: it is visible from the vocabulary alone, without any corpus. What went away is my claim to have measured its value, and the anti-conditions are now the better-evidenced half. Two corrections since this record was first written, both from running Compiler.assess rather than reading ir/vocabulary.py. First, the earlier claim that 'split-K with a declared merge is inexpressible' was too broad: intra-CTA split-K is expressible and the corpus already carries one, with TMA producers and warp specialization. Second, the probe separates three refusals that had been collapsed into one: a device-scope online softmax raises SCHEDULE_STRUCTURE 'admitted values are cta' (missing vocabulary), TMA on a runtime-indexed gather raises ACCESS_INDEXED_MOVEMENT_UNLOWERABLE (a hardware-coherence refusal that is correct -- a descriptor cannot gather scattered page_size=1 rows), and TMA on a contiguous load raises TRITON_LOAD_MOVEMENT (a route capability, not an IR gap, since the native route admits it).
proposed_change: Scope any future proposal to the cross-CTA case alone: a Schedule that declares a partial result and the merge that combines it across CTAs or launches. Do not propose a device-scope ReductionScope member as the whole answer, and do not propose anything for intra-CTA split-K, warp specialization or TMA staging, which corpus/schedules/tinygemm2-stage4-split-k.json already expresses. The positive evidence still does not exist: the corpus has no attention candidates that differ in whether they split under one arm on one task. The 94 SOL-ExecBench L1 tasks include 20 attention captures and remain the natural held-out set, which is a second reason to land the solx_l1 import ADR 0065 specifies. Until that contrast exists this stays a case.
